title: PicardExternalCoefficientsAffineCechDifferential
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ and $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $U:I\to\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ an arbitrary family, and $V\subseteq Y$ any open. Put $W=\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}V$, $E=(\operatorname{pr}_1^*F\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*G)|_W$ [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], $U'_i=W.\iota^{-1}(\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}U_i)$, $L$ the additive-group native Cech complex of $E$ on $U'$, and $D$ the additive-group termwise tensor of the scalar-restricted Cech complex of $F$ on $U$ with $N=\Gamma(V,G|_V)$ [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]. Suppose degreewise isomorphisms $e_n:D^n\cong L^n$ are given and satisfy the pure-tensor section normalization defined by [lem-sc-picard-external-coefficients-affine-cech-terms]: each coordinate of $e_n(a\otimes t)$ is the tensor section of the restricted pullback-unit images of the coordinate of $a$ and of $t$. Then $d_L^{n,m}\circ e_n=e_m\circ d_D^{n,m}$ for every pair related by the upward cochain shape. No finiteness of $I$, affine hypothesis, quasi-coherence, or covering condition is required. This statement asserts no existence of the degreewise isomorphisms.

source.place: varieties-lemma-kunneth, affine-open paragraph, equality of Cech complexes; face restriction compatibility, with Tag 01CD lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: Project to each tuple of length n+2. The Cech differential is its finite alternating face sum. On a tensor a tensor t, normalization gives a tensor section of pullback-unit sections. Restriction of a tensor section is the tensor of restricted sections. Pullback-unit naturality identifies the restricted first section with the unit applied to the face restriction of the coordinate of a; the second section is the unit of the same t restricted from V. Thus each face square commutes, including repeated indices. Additivity gives equality of alternating sums. Tensor induction extends to every tensor and coordinate extensionality gives the square. Non-adjacent differentials are zero by the shape. Empty tuples and zero sections satisfy these identities.

theorem picardAffineCech_normalized_differential
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) {ι : Type w} (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens)
    (e : ∀ n, (picardAffineCechRight f g F G U V).X n ≅
      (picardAffineCechLeft f g F G U V).X n)
    (he : PicardAffineCechNormalized f g F G U V e) :
    ∀ n m, (ComplexShape.up ℕ).Rel n m →
      (e n).hom ≫ (picardAffineCechLeft f g F G U V).d n m =
        (picardAffineCechRight f g F G U V).d n m ≫ (e m).hom
